rules: Desktop composition may be multi-column, but mobile content must retain logical reading order.
Three- and four-column information grids should collapse progressively; avoid preserving desktop-width cards on mobile.
Primary and secondary CTAs may sit inline on desktop but should wrap or stack when their labels would overflow.
Typography must use responsive role tokens rather than fixed desktop pixel sizes.
Section vertical and horizontal spacing should decrease deliberately on tablet/mobile rather than remain desktop-sized.
Images and video must preserve useful subject framing; use object-fit cover for photographic cards and contain for logos/brand marks.
Avoid fixed widths wider than the viewport, horizontal scroll, clipped headings, and off-canvas decorative elements that obscure content.
Tables/comparisons need an explicit small-screen strategy such as stacking or contained horizontal scrolling.
Navigation must use the product's responsive header behavior; page Sparks must not invent a second mobile navigation.
Interactive sliders/carousels need usable touch targets and must not rely on hover-only discovery.
